clue.text: Invaluable? That's absurd

definitions.meaning: something invaluable is beyond any price, too precious to put a figure on
a colloquial exclamation meaning hilariously ridiculous

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: worth more than money can buy, and as slang, so ridiculous it is hilarious.

clue.text: Dismissed for leak

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batter is out when the ball breaks the wicket before they reach the crease
to leak is to drain away until nothing remains, as supplies do

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a cricket dismissal: a batter caught short of the crease while taking a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket method of losing a batter, and a phrasal verb for liquid escaping or supplies becoming exhausted.

clue.text: Force company to speak Irish

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the word for Irish is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A firm is compelled to use the Irish language.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is a dated term for the Gaelic of Ireland and Scotland; 'speak' hints at saying the word out loud rather than at chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone by pressure or threats is a synonym of making them do something.

clue.text: Most up-to-date, or most behind time

definitions.meaning: the newest or most recent of something
the superlative of tardy, arriving furthest after the expected hour

explanation.surface: A thing can be the newest version or the one running worst behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative used both for the newest arrival and for whoever is tardiest.

clue.text: Pride being seen in this wicked group

definitions.text: Pride being seen in this wicked group

parts.words: Pride being seen in this wicked group
parts.note: pride is listed among the gravest moral failings of Christian teaching, alongside greed, lust and envy; a pride of lions is a decoy reading

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' tempts as a group of lions, but here it is the vice, one of a famous set of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Christian list of capital vices, which includes pride, envy, wrath and gluttony.

clue.text: At a stretch, one could be depressed by circus act

definitions.text: At a stretch, one could be depressed by circus act

parts.words: At a stretch, one could be depressed by circus act
parts.note: a taut cable is stretched, and it sags when a performer walks along it; 'depressed' suggests sadness but means pushed down

explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed' reads as gloomy, but it means pressed downwards by the weight of the balancing performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The taut high wire that acrobats walk across in a big-top performance.

clue.text: Skilfully deal with lapse made by scientific expedition

parts.note: to field questions is to handle them deftly
a trip is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone smoothly handles an error committed by a research team on location.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing by students or researchers to study something in its natural setting.

clue.text: You and I want rigorous first entry requirements for European

parts.note: you and I together are we
stern means strict or rigorous

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words entry and requirements are taken

explanation.surface: We face tough entry criteria imposed on a visitor from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' applies to both following words, giving E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A European is a person from the West, as opposed to the East, in the traditional cultural divide.

clue.text: I show amusement about comparison

indicators.note: about here means around, so the expression wraps the letter I

parts.note: to smile is to show amusement

explanation.surface: A person describes laughing at a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that likens one thing to another using 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: In a small coin I have inducement

parts.note: taken as written
a cent is a small coin worth a hundredth of a dollar
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone offers a tiny coin as a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A motivating reward that encourages someone to act is a synonym.

clue.text: Conversation around the French house

indicators.note: the word for conversation goes around the French article

parts.note: a chat is an informal conversation
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Talk turns to a French house.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss-style wooden dwelling, a kind of home in the mountains.

clue.text: Swallowing grains

parts.note: wet ground made of fine particles that engulfs whatever sinks into it; 'swallowing' sounds like eating cereal

explanation.definitionFit: Loose waterlogged sand that sucks down and engulfs anyone who steps on it.

clue.text: Decrepit car runs into a big hole

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, rickety vehicle
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A battered old car drives into a massive pothole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrepit' looks like an anagram signal for CAR, but 'Decrepit car' is the slang word for a banger.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowl-shaped cavity, such as one left by a meteorite or bomb.

clue.text: Lunar? They might be

indicators.note: might be suggests these letters could be reshaped into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Things relating to the Moon could be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging LUNAR plus THEY gives the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: things of the Moon are not of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar matters are literally not of the Earth, so they are otherworldly.

clue.text: Keen-eyed old boy, a hired hand

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a servant is someone employed to work for another

explanation.surface: A sharp-sighted former pupil works as a paid helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchful and quick to notice things, alert in perception.

clue.text: Slip, having to control old calculator

parts.note: to slide is to slip
to rule is to govern or control

explanation.surface: A slip in managing an outdated adding machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-electronic device with sliding logarithmic scales, used for arithmetic before pocket calculators.

clue.text: Almost spring in meadow

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped from the word for spring

parts.note: to spring is to jump or leap

explanation.surface: Nearly springtime in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Pope's astrological sign

definitions.meaning: several popes have taken the name, among them the Great, a fifth-century pontiff
the zodiac sign of the lion, for birthdays in late July and August

explanation.surface: Asking which zodiac sign the pontiff has.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal name used by thirteen pontiffs, and the fifth sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: A church expert

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled person, a crack hand at something.

clue.text: Pacific award, but presented in Scandinavia

definitions.text: Pacific award, but presented in Scandinavia

parts.words: Pacific award, but presented in Scandinavia
parts.note: pacific means peaceful, not the ocean; this honour for peacemaking is presented in Oslo, Norway

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' suggests the ocean, but here it means peaceable; the honour is the one handed out in Norway each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual international honour for work towards peace, awarded in Oslo.

clue.text: Had obligation to recite poem

indicators.note: reciting means saying aloud, so the word is heard

parts.note: owed means had a debt or obligation

explanation.surface: Someone felt bound to read a verse out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric verse addressed to a subject, often in elevated style.

clue.text: List to perish in the stove

indicators.note: in places the word for perish inside the word for the stove

parts.note: an Aga is a well-known British brand of heavy cooking range
to end is to die or perish

explanation.surface: A list of items destined to burn in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a large cast-iron cooking range found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of items to discuss at a meeting.

clue.text: Sailor takes a liking at first to wild animal

parts.note: jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of the word liking

explanation.surface: A seaman develops a fondness for a creature of the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild dog-like scavenger of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Decline to leave university

definitions.meaning: in British usage students ... when they leave Oxford or Cambridge at the end of term or for good

explanation.surface: Someone's fortunes fall as they quit their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British: leaving Oxford or Cambridge is going down, arriving is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to sink or drop, and the traditional term for leaving a university.

clue.text: Fixed up by tailor

parts.note: provided with a set of matching clothes, or simply found appropriate; a tailor kits a client out in jacket and trousers

explanation.definitionFit: Being fitted with a made-to-measure outfit, and also being appropriate or well matched.

clue.text: A guy's gone off to house of worship

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has left for a place of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of A GUYS GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish place of prayer and religious study.

clue.text: In outskirts of town, maintain pub

indicators.note: in puts the word for maintain inside the selected letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of town are used

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: Someone insists on an inn at the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives T and N, and 'In' places AVER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or public house serving drink.

clue.text: Two white things which youngster cuts

definitions.text: Two white things which youngster cuts

parts.words: Two white things which youngster cuts
parts.note: both halves name white things, a drink and part of a smile; a child cuts its first baby teeth

explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as slicing, but babies are said to cut a tooth when it breaks through the gum.
explanation.definitionFit: A first, temporary tooth of a child, later replaced by an adult one.

clue.text: Portrait painter keeps on without friends

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the painter's name surrounds the word on

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century court portrait painter in England
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist carries on painting alone.
explanation.walkthrough: LELY is Sir Peter Lely, portraitist to Charles II, a frequent crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated and solitary, having no companions.

clue.text: Walk by sea pleased an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stroll along the seafront pleased an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade where people stroll.
